messages.subject: stan cmd messages
parts:
Hi,

Can somebody explain what those messages mean (produced by sample):
Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:
Exception thrown at line 202: integrate_ode_bdf: parameter vector[1] is 1.#INF, but must be finite!

Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:
Exception thrown at line 202: CVode failed with error flag -4

When I tried variational inference on the same model it stopped on CVode failed with error flag -4.

Thank you,
Linas

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] stan cmd messages
parts:
Hi Linas,

I can try, but you'll have to dig into Sundials for the exact answer.

On Feb 21, 2017, at 5:33 PM, Linas Mockus <linasm...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi,

Can somebody explain what those messages mean (produced by sample):
Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:
Exception thrown at line 202: integrate_ode_bdf: parameter vector[1] is 1.#INF, but must be finite!

Under Windows, IEEE infinity values are printed as "1.#INF". That means that the first value in your parameters is infinity and the integrate_ode_bdf() call from Stan stopped before it tried to call the CVode BDF integrator.

That's a good thing. I don't know what the behavior of CVode is with parameters that don't make sense.

Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:
Exception thrown at line 202: CVode failed with error flag -4

That's a CVode error. I'm looking through their doc, but wasn't able to find it easily. If you find it, can you post what it is?

Under the hood, integrate_ode_bdf() is calling CVode's solver. We haven't done too much error handling of CVode, mostly because we couldn't set up simple tests that triggers all of the error conditions. If you're seeing  a lot of error codes, let us know and we can wrap the CVode error.
When I tried variational inference on the same model it stopped on CVode failed with error flag -4.

I'm sure the parameters are being pushed into a space where the CVodr integrator fails in a similar way. 


Thank you,
Linas

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] stan cmd messages
parts:
The CVODE user guide is quite good. The error messages are
detailed in Appendix B.2,

CV CONV FAILURE -4 Convergence test failures occurred too many times during
one internal time step or minimum step size was reached.

Combined with the infinity warning, it’s clear that you’re trying
to solve a system of ODE with extreme parameter values that
frustrate the numerical solver. I’m guessing a highly non-identified
system with priors that are far too diffuse.

messages.subject: Re[2]: [stan-users] stan cmd messages
parts:
Thanks for the explanation. Those messages occur during warmup (200) and
then no more messages during sampling (1000). Probably nothing to worry
about. There are up to 100 divergent transitions but hopefully those are
not related. I have 3 chains and Rhat<1.01. I wanted to run variational
to compare results but it broke after -4 message. System is very stiff
so it is very likely that during warmup minimum step size is reached.

Linas
